interactions.summary: The student rereads the reversed arrow passage, and Jiang elaborates that Dante's inversion collapses ordinary sequence to show an event happening beyond human perception in a realm where time and space fall away.
A second student proposes that the reversed order foregrounds the goal first, because willing the end precedes the means, and Jiang warmly accepts that as another valid poetic explanation.

speaker_notes.note: The student's reading and paraphrase of the line remain blended together in one segment, so the exact translation wording is not perfectly separable from the student's gloss.

claims.claim: Jiang interprets Dante's reversed arrow sequence as a poetic collapse of time, where the normal progression of leave, fly, and strike no longer holds.
He says the line can be read at the most basic level as an attempt to render an event happening so quickly that it exceeds human perception and human logic.
A student proposes, and Jiang accepts as plausible, that Dante's inversion puts the goal first because willing the end organizes the sequence that follows.
claims.temporal_scope: Classroom interpretation offered on 2026-06-18 and affirmed by Jiang as one valid reading.

signature_moments.moment: Dante's line is read as if the arrow hits before it even leaves because paradise breaks sequence itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I first hit my target, then I fly, then I leave
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang preserves the heat of the line by treating the disorder as revelatory rather than as a mistake in mechanics.

signature_moments.moment: The end comes first: will and aim organize the path backward from the goal.
signature_moments.source_phrase: where there's a will, there's a way
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This supplies a second live model for the same Dante line, shifting the focus from speed to teleology.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's explanation for poetic inversions in Paradise when events exceed ordinary temporal sequence and human perception.

chronology_notes.note: The student's teleological reading explicitly reaches back to a prior class phrase, 'where there's a will, there's a way,' showing that this lecture builds on an already ongoing conceptual thread rather than starting fresh.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student mentions being inspired by commentary, but the external source is unnamed and should not be treated as independently grounded evidence beyond the classroom exchange.
